look.why: A warm tropical terracotta-amber that resonates with Borneo's sunlit rainforest canopy and complements the rich rufous coat.

size.measure: standing height about 1.2–1.4 m (adult males 1.2–1.4 m tall with arm span over 2 m per ADW)

habitat.text: Lowland tropical dipterocarp rainforests and peat-swamp forests across the island of Borneo.

diet.text: Durians, figs, jackfruit, lychees, young leaves, bark, honey and termites—eating over 400 plant species.

facts.text: The largest tree-dwelling mammal on Earth, weaving a fresh leafy sleeping nest high in the canopy every night.
Its name comes from Malay 'orang hutan', meaning 'person of the forest'; arm span reaches over 2 meters.
